scoring_justification: Recomputing from raw artefacts is infeasible because the agent only submits fitted K0 and compressibility values; the raw P–V data used for the fits is not submitted. Therefore the checker compares the submitted values to the paper-reported reference with tolerances.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold bulk moduli, axial/volume compressibilities, and subset classification for each carbonate, taken from Table 2 of the paper and the paper's discussion of cation valence electron subsets.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Table 2 (K0, b_a, b_c, b_V) and text describing alkaline earth vs. 3d vs. 4d classification.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted directly from the paper's published values; classification follows the paper's own grouping (alkaline earth: Mg, Ca; 3d: Ni, Co, Mn, Zn; 4d: Cd).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: All values are the actual paper-reported numbers for the exact same compounds and units used in the agent's task, ensuring the reproduction target is authentic.

required.carbonates: array of objects, each with keys: carbonate (string), K0_GPa (number, GPa), K0_err (number, GPa)

outputs.description: Room-temperature bulk modulus K0 and fitting uncertainty for each carbonate, obtained from a second-order Birch-Murnaghan EOS fit with K0'=4.

required.carbonates: array of objects, each with keys: carbonate (string), ba (number, 1e-3 GPa⁻¹), bc (number, 1e-3 GPa⁻¹), bV (number, 1e-3 GPa⁻¹)

outputs.description: Mean linear compressibilities b_a, b_c, and b_V derived from linear fits of normalized axes and volume versus pressure.
Classification of carbonates into three subsets based on the cation's valence electron character (alkaline earth s², 3d transition metal, 4d transition metal).

output_contract.notes: FeCO3 is mentioned in the paper but is not included in the provided P–V data; classification includes only the carbonates for which data is supplied. The classification is based solely on cation type, not on numerical trends.
